clue.text: Railing is included in joking

indicators.note: one thing included in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: joking talk is banter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is being mocked as part of a bit of light-hearted ribbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railing' looks like a verb meaning ranting, but it is the definition: a handrail on a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running up the side of a staircase, a kind of railing.

clue.text: Motet, Palestrina's last, contains a curse

indicators.note: the first piece holds the next one inside it

parts.note: a motet is a sacred choral work, like an anthem

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the composer's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Renaissance choral piece by Palestrina turns out to carry a malediction.
explanation.walkthrough: The A from the end of Palestrina goes inside ANTHEM to give ANATHEM, then 'a' supplies the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical damnation, so it is a solemn malediction.

clue.text: A hotline, scrambled for show

indicators.note: scrambled letters are mixed up, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A telephone hotline is jumbled for the sake of appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. IOLANTHE is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, a stage production of the kind called a show.

clue.text: Pulls student up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a swot is a studious pupil, British slang for one who studies hard

explanation.surface: Someone yanks a pupil to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow is to drag along behind, so it means hauls or draws.

clue.text: New cadet, or old soldier

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A choice between a raw recruit and a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCOAT is the old nickname for a British soldier, from the red uniform jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoat was the name for a British infantryman of past centuries, from the scarlet tunic.

clue.text: In watery surroundings, earth tending to smear

indicators.note: in, with surroundings, puts the earth piece inside the watery one
the watery word forms the surroundings, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: serous means watery, like serum
land is earth, ground

explanation.surface: Soil sits in a bath of water, apparently liable to smudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smear' here means defame, not smudge; SEROUS describes watery fluids like serum.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanderous words defame someone, and to smear a person is to defame them.

clue.text: Short of time, encourage to pretend

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so this letter is removed

parts.note: to stimulate is to encourage or spur on

explanation.surface: With no time to spare, someone is urged to fake it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate is to imitate or feign, which is what pretending means.

clue.text: In the country, noticed inferior sort of grape

parts.note: in rural dialect 'I seed it' is used for 'I saw it', so seed means noticed
less can mean lower in rank, inferior

explanation.surface: A rural visitor spotted a poor variety of grape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' marks a rustic usage: country speakers say 'seed' for saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedless grapes are a cultivated type bred without pips, a familiar variety.

clue.text: Laud's group of over two dozen is in private box

definitions.note: read as 'Laud is', the 's standing for is as a link, leaving the verb laud

parts.note: the European Union has over two dozen member states

indicators.note: in puts this piece inside the other

parts.note: a loge is a private box in a theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: Archbishop Laud's party of more than twenty-four people sits in a private theatre box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laud' looks like Archbishop Laud, but it is the verb to praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogise is to praise highly, which is what laud means.

clue.text: Holy Week's midpoint greeted so?

indicators.note: midpoint places the letter in the middle of the other word

parts.note: to greet with a 'hallo!' is to have halloed
W is an abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: In the middle of Holy Week, someone is welcomed in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: W, short for Week, goes into the middle of HALLOED, 'greeted so' meaning greeted with 'hallo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or sanctified, as in 'hallowed be thy name'.

clue.text: Mix up three common elements and start to build

parts.note: C, O and N are the symbols for carbon, oxygen and nitrogen, three common chemical elements
to found something is to establish it, start building it

explanation.surface: A chemist muddles three everyday elements and begins construction.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to confuse or mistake one thing for another, a synonym of mix up.

clue.text: I level slope on trail, say, that gives a measure of warmth

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the I and slope pieces follow the trail piece
say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves
taken as written
to grade is to level a slope, as with a road

explanation.surface: A road builder levels the gradient on a path, in a sentence about thermometers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: the scent of a trail sounds like a cent. 'that gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Centigrade is the temperature scale, an old name for Celsius, used to gauge heat.

clue.text: Hearty pull needed for this?

parts.note: a hearty pull is a strong tug, and the question wants the phrase that describes such a vigorous effort, also a sound bloodline

explanation.definitionFit: A strong heave is a vigorous effort, and strain also means a pedigree line, hearty in the sense of robust.

clue.text: Spend less in bar

definitions.meaning: to spend less money is to economise
bar as a preposition means except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions; 'bar' looks like a pub but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: To save is to economise, and save as a preposition means except, as does bar.

clue.text: Office staff assume this is Philip's place

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of office
to don clothes is to put them on, to assume them

explanation.surface: Office workers suppose this is where Philip works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this is' is a link. Philip II, father of Alexander the Great, was king of the ancient kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedon was the ancient Greek kingdom ruled by Philip II, so it was his realm.

clue.text: Dogs' size inhibits argument

definitions.note: the apostrophe stands for 'are' as a link, leaving the plural dogs

indicators.note: inhibits is read as holds in, so the first piece contains the second

parts.note: mass is bulk or size
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: The bulk of some dogs stops them squabbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are a breed of large, powerful hounds, so they are dogs.

clue.text: Serpentine staff having reason shortly to arrest Fascist leader

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the first piece holds the second
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a cause is a reason
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, the Italian Fascist leader

explanation.surface: A staff of office has grounds to detain Mussolini.
explanation.walkthrough: CAUSE less its last letter is CAUS, which holds DUCE. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The caduceus is Hermes' herald's wand twined with two snakes, a staff wound with serpents.

clue.text: Require addition to letter —- it may assist delivery

parts.note: to force is to require or oblige
PS, postscript, is added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A request for a postscript on a note that will help the post get through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' means childbirth, not post.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are surgical tongs used by obstetricians to help a baby out during childbirth.

clue.text: I have backbone, but I left singers before gig

indicators.note: left is read as departed, so this letter is removed

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers
taken as written
a date is a booked engagement for a band, a gig

explanation.surface: A performer with courage says they quit the choir before a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link. The 'I' of the definition is the creature speaking; the second 'I' is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A chordate is an animal with a notochord or spine, so it can claim to have a backbone.

clue.text: Super ale drunk, providing this?

indicators.note: drunk suggests being in a disordered state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Downing some excellent beer, and what it gives you.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a great beer, drunk, brings enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking a fine beer brings enjoyment, so the clue as a whole describes delight.

clue.text: Sort of scale model finally used in stretch of track

indicators.note: used in means put inside, so the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: a siding is a short stretch of railway track off the main line

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word model

explanation.surface: A model railway enthusiast sets a scale model on a stretch of track.
explanation.walkthrough: A sliding scale is a scale of charges that varies with circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding scale is one that moves up or down with conditions, so it is a kind of scale.

clue.text: Son's fuss about drink

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ado is fuss

explanation.surface: A boy makes a scene over a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is fizzy water or a soft drink, a type of beverage.

clue.text: Shop staff owe man less in change

indicators.note: in change suggests the letters altered into a different form

explanation.surface: Shop workers are owed less by a man in coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Saleswomen are female shop assistants, who work as staff in a store.

clue.text: Suffered taking Indian extremely spicy — I had to leave it

parts.note: IN is an abbreviation for Indian

indicators.note: to leave it means this letter departs from the word

parts.note: curried food is extremely spicy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner found the Indian takeaway so fiery they had to leave it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link; 'I had to leave it' removes the I from CURRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or loss is to sustain it, so incurred means suffered or underwent.

clue.text: Mist over back of hill — difficulty climbing round

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the first piece encloses the second
climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: back of asks for the final letter of the word hill

explanation.surface: Fog hangs over the far side of a hill, an obstacle for those climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link. RUB climbing gives BUR, which goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is a hazy or indistinct shape, much like mist.

clue.text: Working together to beat Nile fever

indicators.note: to beat is to batter, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever

explanation.surface: Collaborating to defeat a disease from the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue was cut short; the page continues 'Nile fever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in league with someone means acting in alliance with them, cooperating closely.

clue.text: Following European that's run off — just like the damned man

indicators.note: off means removed, so this letter goes

parts.note: an Austrian is a European
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Trailing a European who has fled, just like a doomed soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is a link. Faust sold his soul to the Devil and was damned.
explanation.definitionFit: Faustian means relating to Faust, who traded his soul and was damned for it.

clue.text: Weedy type Jesus was mistaken for

definitions.meaning: a person who deals with weeds in a garden
in John's gospel Mary Magdalene took the risen Jesus for the man who kept the garden

explanation.walkthrough: 'Weedy' looks like feeble, but it means concerned with weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener tends plants and pulls up weeds, and Mary Magdalene took Christ for one at the tomb.
